title: What are Functions?
overview: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform a specific task. They help organize code, reduce repetition, and make applications easier to maintain.

title: Creating and Calling Functions
overview: A function needs to be created before it can be used. Calling a function executes the code written inside it.

title: Function Parameters and Arguments
overview: Parameters allow functions to receive values, while arguments are the actual values passed when calling a function.

title: Return Statement
overview: The return statement sends a value back from a function. Returned values can be stored in variables or used in other operations.

example.title: Return Example

title: Arrow Functions
overview: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing functions. They were introduced in ES6 and are commonly used in modern JavaScript applications.

title: Anonymous Functions
overview: Anonymous functions are functions without a name. They are commonly used as callbacks and passed directly as arguments to other functions.

title: Callback Functions
overview: A callback function is a function passed as an argument to another function and executed later when a specific operation completes.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned about functions, creating and calling functions, parameters, return values, arrow functions, anonymous functions, and callbacks.
